tagline: Match the visual to the business question, not to personal preference

slides.title: The Right Visual for the Right Question
slides.body: Every visual type is optimized for a specific analytical question. Choosing the wrong visual forces users to work harder to extract insight — and can actively mislead.
slides.keyPoint: Always start with the business question, not the data. What is the user trying to understand?

slides.title: Business Requirement → Visual Match
slides.caption: The question determines the visual
rows: How have monthly sales changed over time?
Which region has the highest revenue?
What % of total does each product represent?
How does profit vary by region and category?
Am I above or below my sales target?
How are customers distributed by age and spend?

slides.title: Trend Over Time — Line vs Bar

options.label: Line Chart
options.description: Shows continuous change across time. The slope communicates rate of change intuitively.
pros: Ideal for monthly, quarterly, daily trends
Forecasting and reference lines add context
cons: Harder to read exact values than bars
Not suited for comparing discrete categories

options.label: Bar / Column Chart
options.description: Best for comparing discrete categories at a single point in time.
pros: Easy to compare exact values across categories
cons: Does not communicate trend as naturally as a line

options.label: Donut / Pie Chart
options.description: Shows proportion of a whole. Works best with 3–5 segments — cognitive load increases sharply beyond that.
pros: Good for executive summaries with few categories

options.label: Treemap
options.description: Shows hierarchical composition using nested rectangles. Better than pie for many categories.
cons: Harder to read exact proportions than pie

slides.title: Common PL-300 Visual Selection Traps
bullets: Scatter chart — used for correlation between two measures, NOT for time series
Waterfall chart — shows cumulative effect of sequential positive/negative values (bridge chart)
Funnel chart — shows stages of a process where volume decreases (sales pipeline, conversion)
Gauge chart — single value vs a target range; avoid for dashboards with many KPIs (space-inefficient)
slides.keyPoint: For PL-300: if the question mentions 'trend over time' → Line Chart. 'Compare categories' → Bar/Column. 'Part of whole' → Donut/Treemap. 'Two measures correlation' → Scatter.
slides.warning: Pie charts with more than 5 slices are nearly always wrong on the PL-300 exam. If the scenario has 10 product categories, choose Treemap or Bar — not Pie.
